items.title: THE WRONG NEIGHBOR
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original creature/gameplay concept board for Level 5 of a Roblox Backrooms horror game, NOT a screenshot or finished game asset. Premium cinematic 3D concept art with tactile materials and clear, Roblox-buildable shapes, unsettling uncanny domestic realism rather than fantasy armor. Wide landscape board with one dominant environmental hero image and two clearly separated smaller study panels. Consistent world: ordinary cream and muted sage/dusty-pink suburban houses nested ENTIRELY INSIDE enormous but enclosed rooms, beige/green carpet instead of outdoor ground, white wood trim, black-tinted unlit windows, stacked balconies and wrong-height stairs. Clearly visible tiled dropped ceilings with warm, neutral, cool, dim and dead fluorescent panels. Light comes from shared ceilings only; no lamps on or inside small houses, no glowing windows, no sky or daylight. Restrained empty domestic atmosphere, eerie and readable rather than muddy black. No gore, no weapons, no lab/test-zone branding, no company that created this world, no HUD, no watermark. Clean editorial board framing with a small simple exact English title, no long text annotations.

Design an original main stalker called The Wrong Neighbor: a near-human adult in faded ordinary beige cardigan, washed-out brown trousers and simple indoor slippers, superficially mundane, but exceptionally tall, wrong proportions, long neck, lowered uneven shoulders and long forearms. Tiny subtly asymmetrical human-like face, no giant teeth or stock skull head, no glowing eyes; unsettling because nearly normal. HERO: it stands half-concealed in the open doorway of a small cream house beneath a fluorescent ceiling, fingertips almost scraping the carpet and head bent sideways under the door lintel, distant stacked domestic balconies behind it. One side study: full standing silhouette beside a standard doorway for scale; about 1.6 ordinary adult height. Second side study: same creature slowly turning its elongated neck toward a creaking stair in an adjacent corridor, demonstrating listening before pursuit. Still, believable pose and skin rather than attacking or screaming. Clothing and anatomy remain consistent in all panels. Title exactly "THE WRONG NEIGHBOR".
items.conceptNotes: Tall near-human resident with elongated neck and arms; doorway, scale and stairwell views.
items.qualityNotes: Original board includes a small 1.6x scale label as well as its title. The artwork is a concept, not a rig or size specification.

items.qualityNotes: Clear scale and pose concept; topology, rigging and collision feasibility are not established by the image.

items.title: NOISY SHORTCUTS
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a premium, practical 3D environment/mechanic concept board for a Roblox Backrooms horror game, landscape 1536x1024, not gameplay HUD.
Shared art direction: uncanny domestic suburb architecture entirely INSIDE one endless building. Cream and warm beige plaster houses, muted sage and dusty pink façades, white wood trim, uniformly dark tinted glass in every window, beige and green carpet where outdoor streets would normally be, sparse 1980s domestic furniture. Office suspended false ceilings clearly visible above the houses, fluorescent ceiling panels with mixed warm/cool, dim and switched-off states. Modular, buildable forms and appealing realistic materials with restrained Roblox-realizable geometry; high-end architectural game concept render, not photoreal humans, not Minecraft, not toy block art.
Readable soft interior illumination, eerie liminal stillness, no sunlight or sky, no exterior landscape. No lamps or lights mounted on any house, no glowing windows, no light emitted from furniture. No laboratory or Zyntra branding, no suggestion anyone built the Backrooms. No gore, no HUD, no UI arrows, no logo/watermark. Restrained presentation on a warm charcoal/cream board with thin dividers, ample scene area. The only typography is the requested exact uppercase title in a small clean header; no other words or captions.
Primary request: communicate a meaningful spatial choice between a short noisy route and a longer quiet route through the same indoor carpet suburb.
Composition: ONE large three-quarter slightly elevated architectural hero occupying the top two thirds, with TWO tightly framed cinematic detail panels below. Header text exactly "NOISY SHORTCUTS".
Hero: both routes visibly start at one shared near clearing and rejoin at the very same open doorway in a distant sage house on a raised terrace. The short route runs directly up a modest old wooden staircase, across a loose white wooden railing bridge, past a displaced chair and small sideboard that narrow the shortcut. Uneven wooden treads and slightly loose railing parts show why running creates creaks and rattles. The alternate route is unmistakably longer: a broad continuous padded beige carpet ramp/path gently loops around two cream/pink indoor houses to reach that exact same destination, no obstacles and no required jump. Both choices must be geometrically possible and easy to read; no floating or impossible disconnected walkways. Perspective should let the reader trace both routes without colored diagram overlays.
Lower left inset: close-up of one muted-clothed block-proportioned Roblox-like explorer boot pressing down an aged wooden stair tread, the tread subtly flexing at its joint beside a slightly vibrating railing and chair. Tiny restrained motion emphasis, no drawn sound words.
Lower right inset: the same explorer carefully walking along the quiet deep carpet, heel lowered softly, the continuous long way and distant shared destination readable in the background. No monsters needed. The mechanic is noise versus safety, not damage.
items.conceptNotes: Direct creaking wooden stair/bridge route and longer carpet ramp visually converge at a sage house; lower panels show noisy versus quiet footfall.
items.qualityNotes: Path geometry is illustrative. No new image-level issue found during visual inspection.

items.prompt:

Shared art direction: uncanny domestic suburb architecture entirely INSIDE one endless building. Cream and warm beige plaster houses, muted sage and dusty pink façades, white wood trim, uniformly dark tinted glass in every window, beige and green carpet where outdoor streets would normally be, sparse 1980s domestic furniture. Office suspended false ceilings clearly visible above the houses, fluorescent ceiling panels with mixed warm/cool, dim and switched-off states. Modular, buildable forms and appealing realistic materials with restrained Roblox-realizable geometry; high-end architectural game concept render, not photoreal humans, not Minecraft, not toy block art.
Readable soft interior illumination, eerie liminal stillness, no sunlight or sky, no exterior landscape. No lamps or lights mounted on any house, no glowing windows, no light emitted from furniture. No laboratory or Zyntra branding, no suggestion anyone built the Backrooms. No gore, no HUD, no UI arrows, no logo/watermark. Restrained presentation on a warm charcoal/cream board with thin dividers, ample scene area. The only typography is the requested exact uppercase title in a small clean header; no other words or captions.
Primary request: the existing huge dark mycelium wall colonies become a local reactive noise hazard when disturbed by running.
Composition: THREE clean cinematic story panels arranged left-to-right, the same recognisable indoor cream-house wall and low ceiling in each. Header text exactly "REACTIVE MOLD".
Panel 1: establish a giant realistic charcoal-black fungal colony growing from a damp wall seam, spreading as irregular dense mycelium and tangled branching capillary fibers across the plaster and reaching down onto a small patch of carpet. Not a tree mural, not a printed picture, not mushrooms, not glowing fungus. The middle of the wall remains textured with natural patchy mold, and there is a clearly visible walkable strip of clean beige carpet along its outside border. Show one small Roblox-proportioned researcher silhouette slow-walking on that clean border, enough floor visible to understand it is avoidable.
Panel 2: close, dynamic view of the same explorer running across the brittle floor fibers; their foot breaks dry filaments, and a contained fine grey spore/dust puff rises at ankle and chest level. They cover their mouth/cough, without grossness, injury or gore. The gray puff is small and readable, not an explosion, not magic or luminous vapor. Fibers physically connect to the existing wall colony.
Panel 3: a wider corridor view: explorer by the gray disturbed puff, with a distant solitary unnaturally still Neighbor silhouette just beginning to turn at the far cream-house doorway, attention drawn toward the cough. Keep the Neighbor vague and restrained, no red/glowing eyes, no defined redesign; the subject is the mold mechanic. The clean slow-walking border stays visible in all relevant views.
items.conceptNotes: Three panels show black wall growth, a nearby player reacting to airborne dust and a distant figure noticing the noise.
items.qualityNotes: This depicts a proposed interaction; the image does not establish implemented mold reactivity or gameplay effects.

The only typography is the requested exact uppercase title in a small clean header; no other words or captions.
Primary request: an ordinary cream house subtly changes its internal layout between visits: one doorway disappears, the corridor lengthens, and sparse furniture swaps to mirror positions, while a clearly readable escape passage remains.
Composition: TWO equal, wide, paired 3D interior story panels, same eye-level camera lens, same viewing position, same cream room identity. Small third inset if useful, but the paired room comparison must dominate. Header text exactly "THE SHIFTING HOUSE". No BEFORE/AFTER labels or any other text; use matched composition to explain.
LEFT panel: a mostly empty, unfurnished-feeling domestic interior with warm cream plaster, white wood skirting and doorframes, beige carpet, a visibly low office-tile ceiling with mixed fluorescent panels and dark tinted interior window. A short central corridor leads through an open white frame into another empty room; a second open doorway on the left branches aside. Only two sparse domestic props: a small dark-wood chair and a low plain sideboard positioned on opposite side walls, leaving a generous clear central passage.
RIGHT panel: the exact same house and camera after the uncanny change. The left side doorway is now seamlessly cream plaster with no door or frame, the central open passage is still clearly navigable but extends much farther than physically seems possible, repeating white trim and carpet depth to a softly illuminated empty room. The chair and the sideboard have subtly swapped to corresponding mirror positions. All trim and collision geometry remain plausible, no objects clipping into walls or floating. Slightly altered spacing of the fluorescent ceiling panels reinforces the corridor's impossible new length. One subtle misaligned doorframe deep down the extension is enough; no giant surreal portals or rotating rooms.
Both images must keep the same wall color, material quality, viewing angle and identifiable scuff marks, with ordinary architecture doing the horror. No characters or entity needed, no animated effect, no dramatic glowing portal.
items.conceptNotes: Paired interiors show a vanished side door, a lengthened corridor, and a chair and sideboard changing sides.
items.qualityNotes: Readable paired-room concept; implementation would need safe transitions and preserved escape access.

items.title: LOCAL BLACKOUT
items.prompt:
Premium 3D environmental concept art for a Roblox-realizable Backrooms horror level, composed as a clean professional widescreen concept board, landscape roughly 1536x1024. This is a naturally uncanny found Backrooms place, not a constructed corporate testing facility. All architecture entirely INDOORS beneath visible suspended acoustic tile ceilings with warm/cool/dim/off fluorescent ceiling panels. Warm cream domestic facades, crisp white wood trim and balconies, dusty pink and muted sage accents, uniformly dark grey-green tinted non-glowing windows, beige and muted green CARPET on the indoor streets rather than grass. Intentionally implausible stacked suburban architecture, plausible buildable modular shapes, sparse ordinary domestic furniture, tactile slightly worn materials. Moody yet clearly readable forms and navigable spaces. No sky, sun, outdoor scene, grass, house-mounted lamps or light fixtures, glowing windows, lab/corporate branding, Zyntra signs, gore, HUD, weapons, illegible captions, diagrams full of text, or watermarks.
Concept 07: LOCAL BLACKOUT. Exact title text at the top: "LOCAL BLACKOUT". No other text. Three clean cinematic story panels left to right, separated by narrow understated gutters, depicting a short WARNED LOCAL outage on the SAME indoor suburban street and coherent camera position. LEFT PANEL: the street is reasonably illuminated; the nearest overhead fluorescent panel is noticeably too bright, the slight visual unevenness of worn buzzing tubes foreshadows failure while distant ceiling lights still function. MID PANEL: only this near section loses power; the same ceiling fixture is now dark, neighbouring and far panels remain lit; a first-person gloved hand holding a mundane flashlight enters at the lower edge and its beam reveals the carpet, white railings and cream houses. It must NOT become a pitch-black image: retain readable ambient silhouettes and spatial continuity. RIGHT PANEL: the flashlight now exposes the Neighbor in the middle distance at a cross street between the stacked houses: a very tall, thin, near-human resident, about one-and-a-half door heights tall, ordinary desaturated domestic clothing, slightly too-long limbs, standing very still. His small distant face must feel wrong through proportion and stillness, never a gore monster. Keep him distant and relatively small in the composition, leaving most of the environment visible. Show surrounding district lights still running so the localized outage is unmistakable. Fluorescent panels belong exclusively to the dropped ceiling. The tension is brief warning → local darkness → disturbing glimpse, not a combat attack. Attractive art direction, dimensional deep corridor perspective, restrained atmospheric dust, realistic dark windows. Only exact title LOCAL BLACKOUT; no numbering or panel captions.
items.conceptNotes: Three matched panels show a bright warning fixture, a local outage with flashlight, then a tall Neighbor in the distance; far ceiling lights remain on.
items.qualityNotes: Original contains forbidden household table lamps. Targeted lamp-removal edit was interrupted and produced no corrected file; the original remains selected, with this deviation explicit.

Concept 08: THE LAST HOUSE. Exact title text at the top: "THE LAST HOUSE". A clean three-part concept board: a large hero environment at left covering about two thirds of the width, two supporting insets stacked at right. HERO: the interior of the final strange beige house, a sparse cozy-but-wrong carpeted room with one ordinary low veneer sideboard and an empty wooden chair to the side. White domestic trim, off-axis low doorway in the rear wall, a short offset vestibule beyond. A simple unobtrusive physical three-slot wall mechanism next to the exit takes three collected house-number plaques, in exact left-to-right order 8, 3, 6. Mechanism is worn wood/brass/ceramic with no sci-fi electronics. The solved mechanism opens the low doorway so the painted worn brick-red hand-brushed direction arrows lead around the offset corner toward a narrow downward passage. TOP RIGHT INSET: a beautifully clear close-up of the deliberately EASY visual puzzle. A framed faded family photograph depicts people standing in front of THREE small cream houses; the three houses have large clearly legible door numbers, from LEFT TO RIGHT, "8", "3", "6". Directly under that photograph, the simple three-slot mechanism contains matching collected individual house-number plaques reading LEFT TO RIGHT "8", "3", "6". This visually explains matching numbers from the photo with three tiles found during map exploration. The only numbers anywhere are 8, 3, and 6; no keypad, extra code, arithmetic or text instructions. BOTTOM RIGHT INSET: an attractive architectural cutaway perspective of the now-open offset vestibule and very steep, narrow enclosed carpeted downhill corridor with close cream walls and low ceiling; it bends lower and ends in solid pitch-black darkness. The entrance and upper slope remain readable, red paint arrows point INTO and DOWN the passage, and its final lower reach disappears completely into black. A continuous enclosed passage, not an open staircase or elevator. No creature, pursuit, chase, gore or trap shown in this puzzle board. The whole house and passage remain indoors under dropped ceilings. Exact title THE LAST HOUSE only, plus the purposeful puzzle digits 8 3 6. No other labels or captions.
items.conceptNotes: Photo and physical mechanism clearly show matching 8-3-6 plaques; red arrows lead through an offset doorway into a dark downward corridor.
items.qualityNotes: Original has extra furniture and a table lamp; descent inset is perspective rather than cutaway, with step-like breaks. Intended design is cabinet plus one chair, ceiling lights only, and a continuous smooth steep carpet ramp. Targeted correction was interrupted and produced no corrected file.
